verses.text: A thoughtful psalm of Asaph. God, why have you rejected us forever? Why does your anger smoke against the sheep of your pasture?
Remember the people you bought long ago, the tribe you rescued to be your own. Remember Mount Zion, where you live.
Walk through these endless ruins. See all the damage the enemy has done to your holy place.
Your enemies roared in the place where you met with us. They set up their flags as signs of victory.
They acted like men swinging axes to cut through a thick forest.
They smashed all the carved wood with axes and hammers.
They burned your holy place to the ground. They made the place where your name lives unclean.
They said to themselves, "We will crush them completely!" They burned down every place in the land where God was worshipped.
We no longer see miraculous signs. There are no prophets left. None of us knows how long this will last.
How long, God, will the enemy insult you? Will the enemy insult your name forever?
Why do you hold back your hand, your right hand? Take it out from your robe and destroy them!
But God has been my King from long ago. He brings rescue all over the earth.
With your power you split the sea in two. You smashed the heads of the sea monsters in the waters.
You crushed the heads of Leviathan and gave it as food to the creatures of the desert.
You opened up springs and streams. You dried up rivers that always flowed.
The day belongs to you, and so does the night. You set the sun and the light in their places.
You set all the borders of the earth. You made summer and winter.
Remember, LORD, how the enemy has insulted you, how foolish people have insulted your name.
Do not hand over the life of your dove to wild animals. Do not forget your suffering people forever.
Remember your covenant, because the dark places of the land are full of violence.
Do not let crushed people be turned away in shame. Let the poor and needy praise your name.
Get up, God! Defend your cause. Remember how foolish people insult you all day long.
Do not ignore the shouting of your enemies. The noise of those who rise against you keeps getting louder.
